question: On the frozen BEIR-OOD-Subset-v1 benchmark, does fixed-k Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) achieve higher macro NDCG@10 than min-max linear score fusion (alpha=0.5)?
target_scope: Zero-shot hybrid BM25 + dense retrieval across 5 BEIR OOD datasets
unit_of_analysis: Dataset-level macro NDCG@10 across the 5 frozen BEIR OOD splits
construct_or_estimand: Macro NDCG@10 difference (RRF minus linear score fusion)
measurement: NDCG@10 computed by eval_ndcg.py on frozen split_manifest.json
closest_work: Cormack et al. SIGIR 2009 (W2148972377), Section 2 & Section 3
prior_art_boundary: Cormack 2009 tested in-distribution TREC collections only
rival_explanation: Min-max score normalization preserves magnitude information lost by ranks and outperforms RRF OOD
expected_if_focal: RRF macro NDCG@10 exceeds linear fusion macro NDCG@10 by >= 0.02
expected_if_rival: Linear fusion matches or exceeds RRF on macro NDCG@10
discriminating_test: Paired evaluation of baseline_rrf vs candidate_linear on identical frozen BM25+Contriever candidate lists
falsifying_result: Linear fusion achieves >= RRF NDCG@10 under verified split and metric hashes
indeterminate_result: Metric script or split manifest hash mismatch
pilot: Check split_manifest.json and eval_ndcg.py hashes via check_experiment_manifest.py --verify-files
engineering_diagnosis: All 6 engineering checks passed on frozen evaluator and candidate lists
prior_outcome_exposure: Protocol frozen prior to BEIR OOD test evaluation
